segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Looking up, he saw rich people putting their gifts into the treasury.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He also saw a needy widow putting in two small copper coins there,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and he said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “I tell you truly, this poor widow has put in more than all of them.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For all of these added to the gifts out of their surplus, but she, out of her need, put in all she had to live on.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And when some were speaking about the temple, how it was adorned with beautiful stones and votive offerings, he said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “These things that you are looking at—days will come when not one stone will be left on another that will not be thrown down.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They asked him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Teacher, when then will these things be, and what will be the sign when they are about to happen?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Watch out that you are not led astray. For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am he,’ and, ‘The time has come near.’ Do not go after them.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: When you hear of wars and uprisings, do not be terrified; for these things must happen first, but the end will not come at once.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: There will be great earthquakes, and in various places famines and plagues; there will be terrors and great signs from heaven.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But before all this they will lay their hands on you and persecute you, handing you over to the synagogues and prisons, and you will be led away before kings and governors because of my name.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: This will turn out for you as an opportunity to testify.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: So resolve in your hearts not to prepare your defense in advance,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: for I myself will give you a mouth and a wisdom that none of your opponents will be able to resist or contradict.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You will be handed over even by parents and brothers and relatives and friends, and they will put some of you to death,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and you will be hated by everyone because of my name.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Yet not a hair of your head will perish.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: By your endurance gain your lives.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that its desolation has come near.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Then those in Judea must flee to the mountains, those inside the city must leave it, and those in the countryside must not enter it,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: for these are days of vengeance, so that all that is written may be fulfilled.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Woe to those who are pregnant and to those who are nursing in those days! For there will be great distress on the land and wrath against this people,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and they will fall by the edge of the sword and be led captive into all the nations, and Jerusalem will be trampled by Gentiles until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And there will be signs in sun and moon and stars, and on the earth anguish among nations bewildered by the roar of the sea and the surging waves,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: people fainting from fear and foreboding of what is coming upon the world, for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: When these things begin to happen, stand up straight and lift your heads, because your redemption is drawing near.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he told them a parable:

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Look at the fig tree and all the trees.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: As soon as they put out leaves, you see it and know for yourselves that summer is already near.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: So also you, when you see these things happening, know that the kingdom of God is near.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until everything has happened.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will never pass away.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But watch yourselves, so that your hearts are not weighed down with carousing and drunkenness and the worries of daily life, and that day does not come upon you suddenly

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: like a trap. For it will come upon all who live on the face of the whole earth.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But stay awake at all times, praying that you may have the strength to escape all these things that are about to happen, and to stand before the Son of Man.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: By day he was teaching in the temple, and at night he would go out and stay on the hill called the Mount of Olives.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And all the people would come to him early in the morning in the temple to hear him.

notes.note: The Greek names the coin: the lepton, the smallest coin in circulation in Judea. Two of them together came to roughly one sixty-fourth of a laborer’s daily wage. The point is that the gift was almost worthless in money terms and yet was everything the widow had.

One Greek word lies behind both “nation” and “Gentiles” in this chapter. It means a people or nation, and in the plural it often means the non-Jewish peoples. It is rendered “nation” here and in verse 25, and in verse 24 both “nations” (where the captives are scattered) and “Gentiles” (who trample Jerusalem); a Greek reader heard the same word each time.

The verb is the ordinary Greek word for transferring someone into another’s custody or power. Many versions render it “betrayed” in verse 16, where family members are the agents; that names the treachery the context implies, but it hides the fact that the same word is used in verse 12 and, throughout the Gospels, of what is done to Jesus himself. “Hand over” is the basic sense given in the standard lexicons.

The manuscripts are divided between a command (“gain”) and a future (“you will gain”); the two forms differ by a single letter. The Greek text translated here reads the command, while many modern versions follow the future. The sense is much the same either way: endurance is the means by which life is secured.

The Greek word most often means a person’s life or living self rather than an immaterial part of the person, and that is the sense wherever it is saved, lost or gained. Older versions and some modern ones have “souls” here; others, as here, have “lives”. After the warning that some will be put to death, the life gained is evidently more than physical survival.

Roman armies besieged Jerusalem and destroyed the city and its temple in AD 70. Where Mark and Matthew speak at this point of “the abomination of desolation”, Luke speaks plainly of armies and of the city’s desolation. Scholars disagree about whether this wording reflects knowledge of the event or simply draws on Old Testament descriptions of sieges.

notes.traditional: in the land / on the earth
notes.note: The Greek word means both “land” and “earth”. Because the verse goes on to speak of “this people” and the surrounding verses concern Judea and Jerusalem, it is rendered “land” here; some versions have “earth”. In verses 25 and 35, where the scope is worldwide, the same word is rendered “earth”.

notes.phrase: the Son of Man coming in a cloud
notes.note: The language echoes Daniel 7:13, where “one like a son of man” comes with the clouds of heaven and is given everlasting dominion. In the Scriptures a cloud regularly accompanies the presence of God. A first-century Jewish hearer would have recognized the allusion.

The natural sense of the Greek is the people alive at the time of speaking, and most scholars take it so, differing over what “everything” then covers (the fall of Jerusalem, or also the coming of the Son of Man). Others have proposed “this race” (the Jewish people), “this kind of people”, or the generation that sees the final signs. The traditional rendering is kept because it is what the word ordinarily meant.

notes.phrase: like a trap. For it will come
notes.traditional: For as a snare shall it come
notes.note: Manuscripts differ over the position of the word “for”, and so over where the sentence divides. In the text translated here “like a trap” completes verse 34 (“that day does not come upon you suddenly like a trap”). In the other reading it begins a new sentence: “For like a trap it will come upon all …”. The image probably echoes Isaiah 24:17.

candidates.reason: Recurs across the letters and Revelation, where versions vary between “patience”, “endurance”, “perseverance” and “steadfastness”; readers should see one word.
Means the inhabited world (sometimes in effect the Roman empire) and needs to be kept distinct from κόσμος and γῆ in a consistent way across Luke–Acts, Hebrews and Revelation.
A key term in Paul and Hebrews where “redemption”, “deliverance”, “liberation” and “release” are all defensible, and variation would obscure the link between the passages.
“Vengeance” suggests personal revenge to modern readers, whereas the word denotes the carrying out of justice or punishment; it recurs in Luke 18, Romans 12, 2 Thessalonians, Hebrews and 1 Peter.
Frequent across the New Testament and variously rendered “time”, “season”, “opportunity” or “appointed time”; its relation to χρόνος needs a single policy.

warnings: Verse 19: ψυχή is not rendered with a register form (life; soul; person / people / everyone / human being; living being / living creature; mind; wholeheartedly; keep in suspense) and has no register-exception note.
